records.c: The event's entry from the loader: copies the charsets and the horse's frames from $3000 to $E000, then rides for each player in turn.
Starts a ride: blanks the screen, clears $10 to $7F and the status line, banks out the ROMs, sets up the screen and sprites, the interrupt and the first tune, and loops in the main loop.
The main loop: redraws the trees when their column has moved, the hills when theirs has, and unpacks the horse's frame when it has changed. The interrupt does the rest.
Zeroes $10 to $7F.

Sets up the screen: video bank $C000, the screens at $C400 and $CC00, draws the trees and hills into both, the first state ($2E), the field's colours at $BE00, the sprites' colours and modes, and the colour RAM in bands.
Sets the border, background and two multicolours from eq_colour_regs.
The eight sprites' colours.
The border, background and multicolours.
Writes the page of the field's colour table, $BE or $BF, into the ten operands of draw_field.
Turns off the CIA's timer and interrupts, banks out the KERNAL, points the hardware vector at irq and starts the raster interrupt at line $FC.
The raster interrupt: steps down through six slots, sets the next line and jumps to the slot's handler through the table at $1D91, its low byte written into the operand at $1D8F.
Jumps through the handler table.
The handler table's entry, written by irq.
The six handlers: $1DA3, $1DC7, $1DDA, $1DF9, $1E04 and $1E13.
The last three handlers.
The raster line after each slot: $69, $02, $F1, $9F, $83 and $79.
At line $02, the top: no scroll, the sky's charset and colours; then runs the ride's state, places the sprites, draws the field, plays the music, runs the clock and reads the stick.
At line $F1: the status line's font, black, unscrolled.
At line $9F: the field's charset and colours, scrolled by the course's position.
At line $83: the colours between the trees and the field.
At line $79: shows the screen the trees were last drawn into, scrolled a pixel for every 8 the horse goes.
Sets the fine scroll from A, 38 columns, multicolour.
At line $69: shows the hills' screen, scrolled half as fast as the trees.
Places the eight sprites from the horse's frame: Y, then X plus 24.
Sets the sprite pointers on both screens for the set of sprites the horse was last unpacked into.
Waits for the raster to pass a line.
Sets the memory banks from A.
Selects video bank A.
The CIA's bits for each video bank.
Sets the screen at A times 1024 in the bank.
Sets the screen from A, already shifted.
Writes A into the VIC's memory pointers.
Sets the charset at A times 1024 in the bank.
Reads the player's joystick. Carry clear when it has not changed for four reads, so a held stick is read once.
Reads joystick X: carry set while it is changing, clear after four reads unchanged.
Code and tables nothing uses: a fill, a copy and a table of row addresses.
Runs the ride's state through the handler table at $1F2E, its low byte written into the operand at $1F2C.
The state, written by run_state.
Each state's handler: $2E the name, $30 and $36 the button, $32 the count, $34 the start, $38 riding, $3A a jump, $3C a refusal, $3E a fall, $40 to $44 backing away and turning.
The handlers from state $36.

State $38, riding: counts the faults, reads the course's code under the horse, and by its kind and whether the stick is pushed right either starts a jump, refuses or rides on. Code 5 switches the field to its second charset and colours.
Starts a jump: state $3A, the jump's frames, the tune of a jump.
An RTS nothing reaches.
A refusal, unless the horse has backed away since the last: 20 faults, the count of refusals up by one, state $3C, and the horse stands.
Rides on at the pace: moves the gallop's frame on, faster with the pace; at a standstill the horse stands.
The horse stands: its standing frames.
Moves the horse to its next frame, wrapping at frame_last.
State $3E, a fall: the horse stops and the frames of the fall play; at frame 7 they wait for fire; then the horse stands and rides on.
State $3A, the jump: its eight frames. At the end, a jump whose flags ask for it lands cleanly only with the stick pushed left; otherwise a fall: 6 faults, the count of falls up by one, state $3E.
Two bytes nothing reaches.
A clean landing: back to riding.
State $40: the horse starts backing away, four frames, then moves backward; state $42.
State $42: backs away at pace 1 until up is pushed or the course's code 6 is under the horse; state $44.
State $3C, after a refusal: the horse stands; pulling down backs it away (state $40) and lets it take the fence next time.
State $44: the horse turns to face the fence, then rides on at pace 1.
State $2E: when every player has ridden, back to the menu. Otherwise writes the player's name and GET READY, silences the SID, and with fire up goes to state $30.
State $30: with fire up, state $36.
State $36: fire starts the count.
Blanks the screen and returns to the menu through the loader.
State $32: counts FIVE, FOUR, THREE, TWO, ONE and GO, a word every 30 frames, then clears the clock and the faults; state $34.
Writes seven characters from (X, A) into the status line, from column Y.
The low byte of each of the count's words.
Their high bytes, then the words: GO, ONE, TWO, THREE, FOUR and FIVE.
State $34: up starts the ride; writes FAULTS and TIME on the status line.
Clears the status line, white.
GET READY, then FAULTS and TIME.
DISQUALIFIED.
Reads the course's code at the horse's column, from the map at $9800.
The column in the course's code map, written by fence_under.
The page in the course's code map, $98 plus field_page.
The frame delay of each pace.
The speed of each pace, in pixels: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, and 8 for a jump.
The gallop tune's note length for each pace, written into the tune at $2DE7.

Moves the course on by the speed. At $16CC the ride is finished. Works out the field's column and fine scroll, the trees' (an eighth as fast) and the hills' (a sixteenth), and swaps the screens when a column has moved. Draws the field's ten rows from the column.
Copies 40 columns of the field's ten rows from the map into rows 14 to 23 of the screen, each character's colour from the colour table.

Row 1 of the field: its page in the map, from field_page.
Row 1 of the field: the colour table's page, written by set_colour_table.

Row 10 of the field: the colour table's page, written by set_colour_table.

Unpacks the horse's frame into the set of eight sprites not shown: each sprite a count of empty bytes and its other bytes from the end; then swaps the sets and points place_sprites at the frame's positions.
Copies 40 columns of the trees' five rows from the map at $B901, 192 wide, into rows 9 to 13 of the screen being drawn.
The operands of the copy, written above.
Row 1 of the trees: the column it is copied from, low byte, written by draw_trees.
Row 1 of the trees: its page.
Row 1 of the trees: the screen it goes into, high byte.

Copies 40 columns of the hills' two rows from the map at $BD01, 90 wide, into rows 7 and 8.

The hills' second row: the column, 90 on.
The hills' second row: the screen, high byte.
Copies $3000 to $47FF into $E000, under the KERNAL.
Whichever fire button is pressed first, its joystick is the player's.
Each frame: reads the stick. Before the finish up quickens the pace, to 4, and down slows it; after the finish fire shows the score.
The player riding.
Up: the pace rises, to 4.
Disqualified: writes DISQUALIFIED.
Adds the faults due to the faults and shows them and the clock. 100 faults or more disqualifies.
The two digits of A as characters, high in A, low in X.
The clock, each frame: adds 3 hundredths, so a second of the clock is 33 frames. At 99 seconds the rider is disqualified.
Picks the jump for the fence and the pace from the jump tables: its speed and its flags.
Each fence code's jump table, low byte.
The jump tables' high byte, $26, then the tables: for each pace the speed and the flags of the jump.
The music driver's variables for each voice, 7 bytes apart: the note pointer, its length and the timers.
The high byte of each voice's note pointer.
Each voice's note length.
Each voice's count to its next note.
The music driver's counts of each voice's repeats.
The tune to start, low byte.
Its high byte, zero once the tune has started.
The SID register a $FC code is writing.
The SID registers the driver last wrote.
Each voice's control byte.
Changes the tune when the wanted one has changed, then runs the music driver.
Starts tune X.

The music driver, called each frame: for a new tune reads which voices it uses and starts each at its notes. Then for each voice, when its note's time is up, reads the voice's next bytes: $FF ends it, $FE lo hi jumps, $FD n sets the length of the notes, a byte below $80 is a note (an index into the frequency table, $7F a rest) followed by how many times the set length it lasts, and $FC is followed by pairs of a SID register and its value, until a byte of $80 or more.
Each voice in turn, from the third: counts down its note, repeats the length as often as the note asked, then reads its next bytes.
Two bytes after music_step that nothing reads.
Points voice Y at its notes from the tune's header.
Moves the music pointer on and reads the byte there.
Clears the gate bit of voice X, ending its note.
The offset of each voice's variables and SID registers: 0, 7 and 14.
The SID frequency of each note, low byte then high byte.
The table read one byte on, for the high bytes of the frequencies.
The three tunes' headers: the voices used and each voice's notes.
Each tune's header, low byte.
Their high bytes.
Silences the SID.

The score: on a blank screen the player's name, then either DISQUALIFIED or the total time, the optimum time of 50 seconds, a penalty of a fault for each second over it, the falls and their faults (6 each), the refusals and theirs (20 each), and the total. The total, inverted so fewer faults score higher, goes into the record with its text. In practice asks DO YOU WANT TO PRACTICE AGAIN.
The time penalty: the seconds over 50.
The falls' faults, 6 each.
The refusals' faults, 20 each.
Practice: YES or NO with the stick, fire to choose.
In competition waits for fire up and a fire button, then returns for the next player.
The score's words.
TOTAL TIME:.
OPTIMUM TIME: 50.
TIME PENALTY:.
FALLS:.
FAULTS FOR FALLS:.
REFUSALS:.
FAULTS FOR REFUSALS:.
TOTAL FAULTS:.
DO YOU WANT TO PRACTICE AGAIN.
YES and NO.
